title: project.edit request
description: Apply reviewed changes to a project's annotations. `prepared_output`: `prepare` reports the plan and writes nothing, `commit_reviewed` re-derives it and writes only if the digest still matches. The project is named by the envelope's `project` locator.

edits.description: Applied together: one plan, one set of expected digests, one commit. Splitting them into separate requests would let a document change between two edits that were meant to land as a unit. A plan that removes an annotation another one is about is refused rather than cascaded, unless it removes that one too.

allOf.description: Every edit names what it is about by id, except the two that carry a whole type definition: a type's id lives inside `definition`, where the rest of its shape is, rather than being restated beside it.

A capture is bytes nothing can obtain again, so every field that pins them is required and so is the sentence saying what produced them. `env.sandbox.call` composes that sentence and reports it beside each exported range; a capture with no explanation is refused rather than recorded as media somebody has a copy of.

id.description: The annotation's or resource's id, e.g. `function:init-graphics` or `resource:title-logo`.

name.description: The new name, for a rename; the display name, for a resource. Never part of a resource's artifact key.

kind.description: The annotation kind, for an `annotate`; the resource kind, for a resource edit.

parameters.description: The decode parameters for a resource edit, exactly as `resources.schema.json` spells them for that kind — `width`, `planes`, `count`, `encoding`, and so on. A free-form object rather than nine shapes restated here: the resources schema is the definition, and the operation validates against it before writing, so an unknown or missing field is a refusal. The fields the edit itself names — `id`, `kind`, `name`, `target`, `export`, `notes` — are refused here.

definition.description: One type definition for a `define_type` or `update_type`, exactly as `types.schema.json` spells it for that kind — `kind`, `id`, `name`, and whatever else that kind needs. Whole rather than split into `id`/`kind`/`parameters` the way a resource is, because a type needs nothing derived from the project: it has no target and therefore no digest. The operation validates it against the format's own type vocabulary before writing, so an unknown or missing field is a refusal rather than a document nobody can load.

export_media_type.description: What an export of this resource produces. Defaulted per kind when omitted, and part of the artifact key either way.

notes.description: What produced these bytes. Required for a capture, where it is the only provenance the bytes will ever have; optional prose on a resource edit.

target.description: What an `annotate` or a `comment` is about, tagged by `space` the way a document target is. It carries no `object_sha256`: the digest a target is established against is a fact about the project, derived where the project is, so a caller cannot pin an annotation to bytes the project does not describe. `space: entity` names an annotation instead of bytes, and is a `comment` form only.

classification.description: What the bytes are, for a `region`.

size.description: The captured bytes' length, checked against the file at `path` before anything is written.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the captured bytes, lowercase hex, checked against the file at `path` before anything is written.

path.description: Where the captured bytes were written, relative to the project root. Omitting it registers the pin alone, which verifies as unbound rather than as verified.
